title: The person; the gods enter through the doors of the body (1.2)
hook: the gods are offered a cow, then a horse, as a home, and turn both down. then they see a human being
tomorrow: hunger and thirst ask for a place

segments.voice: Yesterday: in the beginning, the self alone, which looked and said, let me create worlds. Your line was the worlds. Did you notice a small world start with a look and a wish? Day four hundred.

Day four hundred, and the Aitareya has a house-hunting story for you. The worlds are made. The self shapes a cosmic person and draws the great powers out of it: fire, wind, the sun, the moon. Gods. But the gods have nowhere to live. They're adrift, the text says, fallen into a great ocean. And they come back with a request: give us a home. So the self brings them a cow. The gods look it over and say, no, this isn't enough for us. It brings them a horse. Not enough either. Then it brings them a human being.
screen: `THE GODS HAVE NOWHERE TO LIVE.` → `A COW? NOT ENOUGH.` → `A HORSE? NOT ENOUGH.` → `THEN, A PERSON.`

segments.voice: When the gods see the person, purusha, they say: sukritam bata. Well made, indeed! The text adds: the person is truly well made. That's the Upanishad's verdict on the human body. Not a prison. Not a burden. A good piece of work, the house the gods accepted. Then the self says: enter, each into your own place. And no god just walks in. Each one changes shape to fit. Fire becomes speech, and enters the mouth. Wind becomes breath, and enters the nostrils. The sun becomes sight, and enters the eyes. The directions of space become hearing, and enter the ears. Plants and trees become the hairs, and enter the skin. The moon becomes mind, and enters the heart. Death becomes the down-going breath, and enters the navel. The waters become seed, and enter the organ of generation. Read that list slowly and the body looks different. On this map, when you talk, there's fire in your mouth. When you look up, the sun is looking out through you. Your quiet, changeable mind is the moon. Even death has a room in the house, low down, at the navel, doing its work. The Upanishad isn't asking you to worship your eyes. It's saying the great powers out there and the small doors in here belong to one system. The person is where they meet. Perhaps that's why, in the story, a cow wasn't enough, and a horse wasn't enough. They needed a place where speech, sight, mind and the rest could all live together.
screen: `WELL MADE, INDEED!` · `ENTER, EACH INTO YOUR PLACE.` · `FIRE TO SPEECH, SUN TO SIGHT.` · `THE MOON BECOMES MIND, IN THE HEART.` · then, large: `SUKRITAM BATA.`

segments.voice: Two minutes touring the doors. Sit, and bring attention to the mouth, resting closed: in the story, fire lives here, as speech. Then the nostrils, the breath moving: the wind. The eyes, closed or soft: the sun. The ears, taking in whatever sound is near: the directions. The skin, the air on it: the plants and trees. The chest, the heart: the moon, as mind. Then rest in the whole house at once, every door open. The bell holds the time.
The person. Purusha, the human being the gods called well made, the one house where fire, wind, sun and moon could each find their door.
Your line: the gods within. Today, the next time you speak, remember the story's fire in your mouth, and let it be worth the house. Day four hundred.

screen: `DAY 400 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: HUNGER AND THIRST ASK FOR A PLACE.`

howItsDone: In Vedic and later Hindu ritual, the body's senses are linked to deities, and some rites include touching the limbs while reciting mantras, a practice called nyasa, which echoes the idea of the gods dwelling in the body.

fork.setup: you're a god with nowhere to live. you're offered a cow, then a horse. now you're shown a human being. what do you say?
options: too fragile. find us a mountain.
fork.reveal: sukritam bata: well made, indeed! then each god takes a new form and enters its own door of the body.

original.note: Sanskrit puruṣa, the person: the human being the gods choose as their home in Aitareya 1.2.

trapdoor: what you thought: the body is just plumbing.
what it means: in the Aitareya, the body is the house the gods chose, each entering through its own door.
what a scholar hears: sukṛtaṃ bata, 'well made, indeed': and each god transforms to enter, fire into speech, wind into breath, sun into sight (1.2.3–4).

sources.ref: Aitareya Upanishad 1.1.3–1.2.4 (the cosmic person; the gods' home; the gods enter the body)

notes: List of entries in 1.2.4 given from memory: agni/speech/mouth; vayu/prana/nostrils; aditya/sight/eyes; dishah/hearing/ears; oshadhi-vanaspatayah/hairs/skin; candrama/mind/heart; mrtyu/apana/navel; apah/retas/generative organ. Please confirm.
The gods 'fell into the great ocean' (1.2.1) and asked for an abode; their hunger is saved for tomorrow (day 401).
howItsDone mentions nyasa as an echo, not as a claim that it derives from this passage; confirm phrasing.
